fault_notes: The agent fails to use the required opening phrase, "Thank you for calling S-Net", at the beginning of the call. The agent otherwise handles the email account lockout professionally, verifies the customer's identity, investigates the issue, and confirms that access has been restored.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Hello, you're speaking with Daniel at S-Net customer support. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi, yeah, I'm having trouble getting into my email account. It says it's locked, and I can't get past the sign-in screen.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm sorry you're having trouble with that. I'll take a look and see what we can do to get you back in.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks. I've tried a few times now, and it keeps saying the account's been locked for security reasons. I need to check something important.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Of course, I understand. Before I access the account details, I just need to complete a quick security check.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yeah, that's fine. What do you need from me?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Could you give me your full name and the first line of the address registered to your S-Net account, please?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's Oliver Hughes, and the address is 18 Meadow Lane.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you, Oliver. I've matched those details. Could you also confirm the four-digit security PIN on your account?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it's 4826.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Perfect, that's all verified. I'll bring up the email service details now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay. I haven't changed anything recently, so I'm not sure why it's suddenly locked.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's understandable. I'll check the account status and then ask a couple of questions to narrow down what triggered it.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, because I was using it this morning without any problems at all.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can see the email service is active on your account. The lock appears to be on the mailbox sign-in itself.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, so it's not that my email service has been cancelled or anything like that?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: No, not at all. Your service is still active, and we'll focus on restoring your access.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good, because I was worried I'd lost all my messages. I've got a few things in there I really need.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand why that would be worrying. A sign-in lock doesn't normally mean your stored emails have been deleted.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: All right. What do you need to know first?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: When you try to sign in, are you using the S-Net webmail page, an app on your phone, or an email programme on a computer?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Mostly the webmail page on my laptop. I tried the app on my phone afterwards, and that failed too.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thanks, that helps. And are both devices showing the same locked-account message?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Pretty much, yes. The laptop says the account is locked, and the phone just says it can't sign in.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Understood. Have you recently changed your password, or had to reset it on another device?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, not recently. I did try entering my usual password a few times when it didn't work, though.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That may be relevant. Several unsuccessful attempts can trigger an automatic security lock, even if the password is normally correct.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: But I'm fairly sure I typed it correctly. Could someone else have tried to get into my account?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It's possible, although the lock alone doesn't prove that. I'll check the security information available to us before we decide on the next step.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, I'd rather be safe than sorry. I just don't want somebody reading my emails.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Absolutely. I'll review the recent access indicators and help you secure the account as part of getting you back in.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks. I did notice the phone had been asking me to sign in again yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's useful to know. Did you dismiss the prompt at the time, or did you enter your password on the phone?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I entered it once, and it didn't accept it. I left it alone after that until this morning.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So the phone prompted you yesterday, rejected the password, and now both devices are unable to access the mailbox. Have I got that right?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, exactly. That's what's happened.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thanks for confirming. I'm checking the lock status now, and I'll explain what I find before making any changes.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: All right, but is this going to take ages? I've already spent about half an hour trying to sort it out.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can appreciate how frustrating that is, especially when you've already tried several times. I'll keep this as straightforward as I can.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I appreciate that. I just need to know what caused it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The account record shows a temporary security lock following repeated unsuccessful sign-in attempts. I can't confirm whether they all came from your devices.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's a bit concerning, to be honest. Can you see where those attempts came from?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can see the failed attempts recorded, but I don't have a reliable location detail to share with you from this screen.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right. Well, can we at least unlock it and change the password?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes. I'll guide you through the approved recovery process, then we'll set a new password and check that you can sign in.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay. Do I need to give you the new password over the phone?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: No, please don't share it with me. You'll enter it yourself through the secure recovery page.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good, that's what I was hoping you'd say.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: First, open a new browser tab and go to the official S-Net webmail sign-in page. Don't use any link from an unexpected email.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I've got it open now. There's a link saying I've forgotten my password.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's the one to select. It should take you to the secure account recovery options.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, it's asking me to confirm my recovery mobile number. The last two digits look correct.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good. If the number is yours, continue with that option and request the verification code.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I've requested it. Just waiting for the text to come through.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: No problem. Let me know when it arrives, and enter the code directly into the recovery page.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's just come through. I've entered it, and it's accepted.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Excellent. You should now be able to create a new password. Choose one you haven't used for this account before.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, I've entered one and confirmed it. The page says the password has been changed successfully.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Great. Please return to the sign-in page and try logging in with your email address and the new password.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I'm doing that now. It's loading... oh, hang on, I'm in. I can see my inbox.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's good news. Can you see your recent messages, and do the folders appear to be there as expected?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, everything seems to be there. I've got my inbox and sent items, and the latest emails are showing.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Perfect. That confirms webmail access is working again. We should also make sure the phone isn't still trying to connect with the old password.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, I nearly forgot about the phone. Will it update automatically?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It may prompt you to sign in again. If it does, enter the new password directly into the email app.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's asking me now. I've entered the new one, and the error has disappeared.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Lovely. Can you refresh the inbox on your phone and check whether the latest messages appear?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, they're coming through now. That's a relief.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm glad we've got both devices working again. I'd recommend checking your recovery details are up to date while you're signed in.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's sensible. Is there anything else I should do in case somebody was trying to access it?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Use that new, unique password, keep it private, and review any recent security notifications. If you spot unfamiliar activity, contact us straight away.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: All right. I don't see anything unusual in the inbox, but I'll have a proper look at the security notifications later.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That sounds good. And please remember, we won't ask you to tell us your password or read a verification code out over an unsolicited call.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, that's helpful. I'm just glad I can get to my emails again.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Absolutely, Oliver. Just to confirm, you can now sign in on both your laptop and your phone, and the messages are loading correctly?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, both are working. I can see the inbox on each device, and the new password is accepted.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Brilliant. Is there anything else about your email account that you'd like me to check while we're here?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, I think that's everything. You've talked me through it clearly, thanks.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome. I'm pleased we've restored access, and I'd suggest keeping your recovery mobile number current in case you need it again.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Will do. Thanks for your help, Daniel. You've saved me a lot more messing about with it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It's been a pleasure helping you, Oliver. Thanks for your patience while we worked through the recovery steps.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No worries. Have a good evening.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You too, Oliver. Take care, and thank you for choosing S-Net.
